item.title: MRV RATIFICATION
item.description:
Investigation | Special Materials | Notice In plain English (machine-written): The Department of Investigation says the city's chief procurement officer approved ratifying minor rule violations in a negotiated contract with Epstein Becker Green and Kroll Associates to provide investigative services for a City Council-mandated probe of World Trade Center toxin knowledge.

On September 30, 2026, pursuant to Section 1-02(h)(1)(ii) of the Procurement Policy Board Rules ('PPB Rules' or 'Rules'), the City Chief Procurement Officer (CCPO) approved the New York City Department of Investigation's ('DOI') request, dated September 18, 2026, to ratify minor Rules violations for Negotiated Acquisition (ePin 03227N0001) procurement, pursuant to PPB Rules Section 3-04(b)(3) and 3-04(d)(1).

DOI entered a Negotiated Acquisition with Epstein Becker Green, P.C. (EBG) and Kroll Associates (Kroll) who had submitted a joint proposal to provide professional investigative services to assist DOI in the City-Council-mandated investigation to 'ascertain the knowledge possessed by the mayoral administrations on environmental toxins produced by the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center and to subject a report to the council thereon' (the 'Engagement').   The contract term for the Engagement is from November 2, 2026 to July 17, 2027, with (3) one-year (1-year) renewal…

item.description:

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG)

ALTERNATIVE ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM (AEP) 5-YEAR REVIEW - 2026

NOTICE OF INTENT TO REQUEST RELEASE OF FUNDS (NOI RROF)

             

REQUEST FOR RELEASE OF FUNDS

On or about October 8, 2026, the City of New York (the City) anticipates submitting a request to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) for the release of $51,780,000 of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds authorized under the Housing and Community Development Act of 1992, to undertake the Citys Demolition Program citywide, for a period of five years.

The Alternative Enforcement Program (AEP) is intended to address the serious physical deterioration of the most distressed buildings in New York City. Through AEP, the NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) can order the property owner to repair or replace building systems as well as to address violations. item.title: NOTICE OF FILING - 43-58 11TH STREET, QUEENS
item.description:
School Construction Authority | Special Materials | Notice In plain English (machine-written): The School Construction Authority has filed notice of a proposed site at 43-58 11th Street in Long Island City, Queens, for a new 972-seat intermediate school on a roughly 1.08-acre lot.

NOTICE OF FILING

Pursuant to §1731 of the New York Public Authorities Law, notice has been filed for the proposed site selection of all or portions of Block 453, Lot 1 and any other property in the immediate vicinity which may be necessary for the proposed construction of a new, approximately 972-seat intermediate school in Queens.

The proposed site is located at 43-58 11th Street on the north side of 44th Avenue, between 10th Street and 11th Street in the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens. The site is currently occupied by one to two-story commercial and manufacturing buildings. The proposed site to be acquired by the New York City School Construction Authority, on behalf of the New York City Department of Education, is an approximately 47,255 square foot (1.08 acre) lot.

item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Special Materials | Notice

Notice of Concept Paper

The NYC Department of Social Service (DSS)/Human Resources Administration (HRA) is committed to strengthening and modernizing the NYCBenefits Program to promote accountability, workforce capacity, cross-system coordination, and high-quality, client-centered services. The purpose of this document is to:
 

  1. Outline HRAs proposed enhancements to the NYCBenefits service model;
  2. Solicit stakeholder feedback regarding program design and operational requirements;
  3. Assess provider interest and organizational capacity; and
  4. Inform the development of a Request for Proposals (RFP)/RFx.

Anticipated number of contracts: Between thirty-eight (38) and fifty-eight (58), aligned with the following provider specializations:
 

  • Thirty-five (35) to fifty-three (53) Direct service vendors
  • Three (3) to five (5) Technical Assistance vendors

NOTICE OF RATIFICATION OF A MINOR RULES VIOLATION

On August 11, 2026, pursuant to Section 1-02(h)(1)(ii) of the New York City Procurement Policy Board Rules (PPB Rules), the City Chief Procurement Officer (CCPO) ratified a Minor Rules Violation request submitted by the New York City Department of Probation (DOP) in connection with the Negotiated Acquisition Extension ('NAE') for the NeON Arts Program.

The minor Rules violation concerned compliance with PPB Rule §2-11 relating to the timing of the public notice and comment process. DOP and the CCPO determined that the violation had no significant adverse impact on the procurement process and that ratification is in the best interests of the City.

item.title: Community Justice Transitional Network (CJTN) RFP EPIN: 12827P0001
item.description:
Mayor's Office of Criminal Justice | Special Materials | Notice In plain English (machine-written): The Mayor's Office of Criminal Justice is seeking proposals, due through a Request for Proposals released Aug. 18, 2026, to create a Community Justice Transitional Network that helps justice-impacted New Yorkers plan for release and reentry into their communities.

MOCJ seeks to solicit proposals to serve justice-impacted NYC residents in planning for their release and transition into community. MOCJ seeks to do this by establishing the Community Justice Transitional Network which is comprised of three components of service and six competition pools. The first component is for hybrid in-custody/in-community transition services. The second component focuses on comprehensive services in the community. The third component focuses on support for people in an acute rearrest period both in-custody and in-community with specialized and responsive care.

The date of release for the RFP is 08/18/2026 via PASSPort under EPIN12827P0001.  This will be released city wide utilizing the Pre Qualified List (PQL) 

Any questions or concerns please reach out to MOCJ via MOCJProcurements@mocj.nyc.gov
